Context/Background:
Intraductal papillary neoplasms (IPNs),  including intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs), intraductal oncocytic papillary neoplasms (IOPNs), and intraductal tubulopapillary neoplasms (ITPNs), are clinically detectable macroscopic non-invasive cyst-forming lesions, some of which progress to invasive pancreatic cancer. Proteins and glycoproteins have proven to be useful clinical biomarkers for classifying cyst-forming neoplasms in the pancreas.Here, we used proteomics and glycoproteomics to characterize a series of histologically and genetically well-characterized surgically resected IPNs, including IPMNs and IOPNs.

Our analysis included 69 IPNs (64 IPMNs and 5 IOPNs), 76 macro-dissected grossly normal duct tissues (NDs, with 32 of the 76 NDs coming from the same resection specimens as the IPNs), and 32 cyst fluid samples (22 from matched IPMN patients, 3 matched IOPN patients, 2 from unrelated IPMN patients, and 5 other cysts).
Prompt: Look at the differential genes between IPMN and ND samples, provide a summary of enriched pathways in IPMN compared to ND.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
Proteomic profiling (Wang_2025_Cancer_Cell_TableS2A.csv) compared surgically resected IPMN lesions (n = 64) versus grossly normal pancreatic ducts (n = 76). Differential abundance was assessed by log2 fold-change and FDR. Key upregulated proteins in IPMN included mucins (MUC5AC, MUC1, MUC6, MUC13), immunoglobulin light chains, and collagens (e.g., COL8A1), whereas core ribosomal proteins (e.g., RPLP1, RPS19) and digestive enzymes (e.g., PRSS1/2) were downregulated. Replicate numbers, patient demographics, and precise assay platform are not specified.

Keywords  
• Mucin  
• Ribosome/Translation  
• Extracellular Matrix  
• Immune/Phagosome  
• Integrin signaling  

Candidate Genes  
MUC5AC, MUC13, RPLP1, RPS19, FN1, ITGB5

Analysis  
IPMN lesions show concerted upregulation of immune- and matrix-remodeling pathways (e.g., Phagosome, Integrin signaling, EMT, Interferon Gamma Response) alongside downregulation of core translation machinery (Ribosome, Cytoplasmic Translation, rRNA Processing). The downregulation of digestive-enzyme pathways (Pancreatic secretion, Protein digestion) further distinguishes IPMN from normal ducts. Hallmark gene sets highlight strong activation of EMT (FN1, ITGB5, MUC1/5AC) and inflammatory responses. The inverse regulation of translation versus extracellular/immune processes suggests a shift from homeostatic exocrine function toward a pro-tumorigenic microenvironment in IPMN.

Targeted (keyword-guided) subset  
Filtering enriched terms for “mucin,” “matrix,” “immune,” and “translation”:  
| Data Base                  | Term                                 | NES    | Leading Genes                 |

| MSigDB_Hallmark_2020        | Complement                           | 2.794  | SERPINB2, FN1, C1R, CFH, …   |
| MSigDB_Hallmark_2020        | Interferon Gamma Response            | 3.489  | PFKP, CD38, NFKB1, IRF1, …   |
| GO_Biological_Process_2023  | Cytoplasmic Translation (down)       | –5.692 | RPLP1, RPL27, RPS16, …       |
| Reactome_Pathways_2024      | SRP-dependent Protein Targeting (down) | –6.593 | SPCS1, SEC61B, RPS14, …      |

Key Genes/Proteins (leading edge)

Upregulated  
| Gene   | Direction | Role/Function                         | Pathway(s)                                  |
|--------|-----------|---------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| FN1    | Up        | Extracellular matrix glycoprotein     | EMT, Integrin-Mediated Signaling            |
| ITGB5  | Up        | Integrin β5 receptor subunit          | Integrin-Mediated Signaling, EMT            |
| MUC5AC | Up        | Secreted mucin glycoprotein           | EMT, Estrogen Response Early                |

Downregulated  
| Gene   | Direction | Role/Function                         | Pathway(s)                                  |
|--------|-----------|---------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| RPLP1  | Down      | Ribosomal P1 lateral subunit          | Ribosome, Translation Initiation/Termination |
| RPS19  | Down      | Ribosomal S19 subunit                 | Cytoplasmic Translation, Peptide Biosynthesis |
| RPL27  | Down      | Ribosomal L27 subunit                 | Ribosome, rRNA Processing                   |

Comparisons & Confidence  
- Immune/EMT upregulation is consistent across all libraries and FDR-significant.  
- Robust downregulation of translation and secretion pathways (high NES magnitude).  
- Single-modality signals (e.g., Viral carcinogenesis FDR > 0.05) are noted as lower confidence.

Implications  
These shifts suggest that IPMN development involves suppression of normal exocrine/translation functions and activation of pro-matrix and immune processes, potentially driving cyst growth and tumorigenesis. Targeting integrin or EMT pathways—or restoring translational homeostasis—might offer therapeutic angles.

Next Steps & Clarification  
1. Validate key protein changes (e.g., FN1, ITGB5, RPLP1) by orthogonal assays (IHC, western blot).  
2. Determine whether translation repression is due to mTOR signaling or ribosome composition changes.  
3. Assess cytokine/immune cell infiltration in IPMN stroma to contextualize phagosome and interferon signatures.  
4. Clarify the contribution of mucin upregulation to cyst fluid viscosity and clinical biomarker performance.
